evidence: Partly right: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:58 changes the constructor param from InsightsBookingServiceOptions to InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions (a flat type with optional teamId, lines 29-34). That is inconsistent with insightsRouting.ts:52, which still takes InsightsRoutingServiceOptions. It also loosens compile-time safety: {scope:'team'} with no teamId now compiles. The claim of 'no runtime validation' is wrong, though. insightsBooking.ts:62-63 still runs insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse(options) and sets this.options to null on failure, so bad input falls through to NOTHING_CONDITION (lines 89-90), not to unsafe behavior. Reverting the param to InsightsBookingServiceOptions would bring back the discriminated-union typing and match the routing service.

The type is not unused. It is the constructor param type at insightsBooking.ts:58, and no other file references it (grep only finds the definition and that use). The reviewer is right that it is redundant and confusing: the class stores a separately typed InsightsBookingServiceOptions (line 47, from the zod schema at 10-27/36), so there are two near-identical option types. Nothing else needs it, so it can be dropped in favor of InsightsBookingServiceOptions. This overlaps with issue 0.

The PR diff removes the whole describe('Caching') block ('should cache authorization conditions' / 'should cache filter conditions') from packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts, and the file at HEAD has no caching tests. The caching logic is still in the service: insightsBooking.ts:49-50 (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions) and 83-95 (the getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions memoization). The routing service's integration tests still have a Caching describe (lines ~444-494), so dropping these tests also breaks the 'same pattern as InsightsRoutingService' claim in the PR description. They should be restored with Prisma.sql expectations (and ideally a check that the second call returns the same object and doesn't run the build again).
